author: Southeastern Asset Management
title: Longleaf Partners Fund 2Q26 Commentary
headline: Southeastern says markets have gotten crazy: Longleaf made 3.9% while the S&P 500 jumped 15.2%, and it won’t chase the AI winners.
summary: The Longleaf Partners Fund gained 3.87% in the second quarter against 15.20% for the S&P 500 and is down 0.77% for the year; almost 90% of the gap came from owning little technology. Southeastern argues the market has turned more speculative: hyperscaler free cash flow is below 2019 levels on a forward basis, earnings and the CAPE multiple are both further from their long-run averages than ever, and it views the SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI IPOs as it viewed last year’s Fermi IPO. It believes its returns are deferred, not lost: the 17 holdings trade in the high 50s percent of appraised value, with value being unlocked at Fortune Brands, Mattel and People Inc.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Bought one new holding, a healthcare company it has owned profitably before; sold Bio-Rad after another disappointing quarter and the FedEx Freight shares received in the spin-off.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Published a letter to Mattel after private engagement fell short; things have gone well since, though not yet in the share price.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: The extended AI group stays unattractive: money circles between hyperscalers, venture capital and debt-funded buyers and inflates revenue and adjusted EBITDA.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: People Inc.’s bid for control of MGM Resorts. Southeastern likes the idea, but the details will matter.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: FedEx spent only 4% of revenue on capex, the lowest in its history; the market still underrates the cash the parcel network can produce.

risks.text: Both earnings and the multiple on them sit far above long-run averages, so owners of broad indices can lose on both.
Pressure is building in an unstable market structure before something dramatic happens; regulation will then turn stricter.
Regeneron’s pipeline went one for three, and Albertsons faces intense competition from Walmart and Aldi.

quotes.text: We believe that our absolute and relative returns have been deferred, not foregone, with considerably less risk going forward.
now is not the time to chase what has worked, but rather it is the time to go on record that things have gotten crazy.
In short, multiples keep moving up while real earnings power struggles to keep up.
